reused_principles: Canonical JSON content-addressed evidence, immutable originals and bounded decompression.
New storage descriptor preserves all original source semantics and clocks; storage integrity does not certify source meaning or freshness.
storage_design: Every exact original article row version is encoded with the original collector's compact sorted-key ensure_ascii=True JSON encoding, compressed with zlib and keyed by its canonical SHA256.
An ordered list of original row hashes is itself a content-addressed compressed blob. Identical selections reuse the complete manifest, with one capture-to-manifest reference.
Raw envelope metadata and full feature JSON are separate canonical blobs. Reconstruction recreates the original_rows list in exact order, retaining duplicates and original JSON string field bytes.
One source contract, cohort and source-bindings digest per store; canonical UTC context-bucket identity prevents duplicate equivalent-time publications.

SQLite DELETE journal, synchronous=FULL, foreign keys and UPDATE/DELETE rejection triggers protect normal append-only API use. These protections do not authenticate a database against a privileged administrator who can rewrite schema and hashes.

Payload commit precedes a separate read-only connection's full exact reconstruction. The actual subsequent wall clock is recorded in a separately committed publication receipt. A final read verifies the receipt.

An interrupted receipt phase can leave a complete, explicitly unpublished payload. Public read_capture rejects it; recover_pending reconstructs it and records a new current ready clock, retaining the original old context clock.
No broker, network, producer, historical backfill, activation or source-database writes.

capacity_policy.note: Unique logical bytes count canonical blobs once. Database page count separately bounds references, metadata and receipts. Preflight disk reserve includes the existing database size for a worst-case rollback journal plus planned new compressed data. No persistent WAL/SHM is produced. Capacity failures never evict old evidence; transactions roll back or leave only an explicitly unpublished payload if a crash or disk change occurs after phase one.

actual_input_recreation.destination: Disposable temporary SQLite database, removed by test cleanup; no original database modified.
actual_input_recreation.limitation: Per-row compression initially uses more space than compressing one complete snapshot. The measured 8192-byte increment reflects unchanged rows in these two captures, not a guarantee for future article-version churn.
actual_input_recreation.benchmark_note: The previously recorded exact-payload timings/memory/growth were measured before the additive metadata-header helper. Existing publish, deduplication, payload reconstruction and receipt semantics are unchanged by this addition.

memory_optimization.change: Verified readers perform metadata validation directly on exclusively owned decoded blobs, avoiding a second complete copy and write-preparation pass. Every compressed/canonical/full-envelope hash and bound is still checked.
memory_optimization.after_scope: Two complete publish and external-replay operations in one standalone process; excludes root producer and child orchestration.

publication_header_addendum.scope: Metadata only, for startup clock seeding and bounded-child recovery routing; does not read payload blobs or establish full feature authority/freshness.
checks: SQL bounds every metadata field and receipt before fetching.
Stored receipt SHA verified; capture/contract/cohort/raw/feature/source identities and inert flags match the capture metadata.
Context clock is canonical UTC; context <= computation completion <= observed publication.
Missing capture raises capture_missing; pending returns published=false and observed_ready_utc=null.
publication_header_addendum.validation: Three added tests (nine cases) cover no-blob reads, missing/pending, identity/hash/clock drift, and oversized metadata/receipts.
